referees.quote: The work “Magnonic spontaneous oscillation induced by parametric pumping” looks solid and is well written, and may be accepted for publication after the revision.
The general idea is not particularly novel, and the authors could/should articulate the novelty aspect of their work better... their interpretation could benefit from more rigor and depth

note: The file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal, so the first round is Version 0. Neither referee states a recommendation category in round 1, so both are inferred. R1 calls the work solid and acceptable 'after the revision'. R1's requests are mostly clarifications, labels, references and figure fixes, plus one optional supplementary dataset, so this reads as minor revision. R2 finds the results interesting but questions the novelty. R2 also asks for substantially more rigorous interpretation: whether the f-k dispersion was measured or calculated, whether energy and momentum conservation check out, whether phase-locking is rigorously proven, and why the idler mode appears irregularly. That points to major revision. Later rounds are not used for the ratings: R1 recommended publication 'after minor revisions and corrections' in Version 1 and then publication in Version 2. R2's Version 1 report is blank and R2 does not appear in Version 2.
